body:
Hey, I've gone ahead and addressed your notes as well as squashed all the commits. I also thought it would be appropriate to include the original commit author details from the pull request this was based off as a co-author.

The one minor concern I've got at the moment is that the fallback makes error messages a little confusing when many matching solutions are found during export. On a sample project I'm using to test a multi-project solution the multiple matching solution error will get thrown multiple times  and for each C# file these errors will get throw:

`
ERROR: Export .NET Project: This project contains C# files but no solution file was found at the following path: /home/sam/src/godot-net-testing/pathfinding/Demo.sln
A solution file is required for projects with C# files. Please ensure that the solution file exists in the specified location and try again.
`

and

`
ERROR: System.InvalidOperationException: res://Nodes/CameraController2D.cs is a C# file but no solution file exists.
   at GodotTools.Export.ExportPlugin._ExportFile(String path, String type, String[] features) in /home/sam/src/godot/modules/mono/editor/GodotTools/GodotTools/Export/ExportPlugin.cs:line 136
`

This of course being due to the fact that when no matching solution is found the old behavior of assuming a solution file with the same name as the assembly in the specified solution folder is used, but it does not exist. I think having all of these errors show up has the potential of being confusing, but this should only happen if you ignore the multiple solution error in the editor and try to export the project, so I'd like some thoughts on if this case needs any special considerations.

I think it's fine, only a little annoying that we show the error for every C# file instead of only once. But it's the same as before this PR when you were missing the `.sln` file. This error is added here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e1b4101e3460dd9c6ba0b7f8d88e9751b8383f5b/modules/mono/editor/GodotTools/GodotTools/Export/ExportPlugin.cs#L132-L137

I don't think it's within the scope of this PR, so I would leave it as-is.

Alright, I'll just let that be then. I've also just tested this on Windows and updated the path separator handling to work properly. The error message will now also use Unix path separators to match the trace path separators.
Thanks! Congratulations on your first merged contribution! 🎉

Not sure what is the place to ask, but seems like @samuelll3d, might know the most. (Please suggest better place to discuss this)

How does proper multi project setup looks like? Iam trying godot Godot_v4.6-dev4_mono_win64 version that should contain this fix, but still i struggle.
I would expect that I would have 1 sln file, and any structure / number of csproj within the solution or nested directories. (maybe one contrain the entry .csproj would have to match the project name)

This is my structure:
root
--Game
----MyGame.sln
----MyGame.csproj
----project.godot
--Shared
----Shared.csproj
------SharedScript.cs

And MyGame.csproj references the Shared.csproj
In my main scene I assigned Shared/SharedScript.cs to a node

Building works fine, but once i try to run in editor i got this error:
```
E 0:00:00:820   can_instantiate: Cannot instantiate C# script because the associated class could not be found. Script: 'res://Shared/SharedScript.cs'. Make sure the script exists and contains a class definition with a name that matches the filename of the script exactly (it's case-sensitive).
  <C++ Error>   Method/function failed. Returning: false
  <C++ Source>  modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2400 @ can_instantiate()

```
I could workaround it by having this structure (basically all files are part of MyGame.csproj)
But this this has big drawback since all csproj properties/nuget packages of all nested csproj must be in MyGame.csprok too - basically the nested .csproj files are not even used.

root
--Game
----MyGame.sln
----MyGame.csproj
----project.godot
----Shared
------Shared.csproj
--------SharedScript.cs


So i wonder what is the proper multi project structure.

Hey @Basyras. I've been doing some testing and it seems that you won't be able to attach scripts from external projects onto nodes inside of the editor, likely because the engine expects resources like scripts to be inside of it's resources directory, hence your workaround.

That said, I am able to instantiate nodes programmatically from other nodes. Truthfully I wasn't expecting much of this at all to be functional since I only tested with a generic .NET class library that didn't use anything from the Godot libraries, though it does appear to work to some degree despite the scripts not being a part of the Godot project. [This](https://github.com/samuelll3d/godot-csharp-multiproject) is what I was able to come up with.

I don't know that this works well enough to be used for any real projects and the downside of not being able to work with the scripts inside of the editor is quite a major one, though maybe this could be of some use. It is also entirely possible to use other generic .NET code and reference them inside of the actual game project.

All that said, I'd be interested to hear from someone more familiar with the internals of the engine on whether this kind of configuration could be supported properly and how much work it would require.

I see.. good that I am not doing anything wrong :). Well anyway thanks for the test repo and PR!

Yeah, its pitty it is not possible to assign scripts from reference projects. I also tried to set script later, after the node is created but i didnt manage to do that also.
